summary: Shows registering a `poll: 0` async task and waiting on it later with `async_status` using `until: job_result is finished`, retries, and delay. Notes `async` must be long enough for the status file to exist, async tasks always report changed (so `changed_when` belongs on the `async_status` task), and shows batching async tasks with `batch(2)` and include_tasks.
questions: How do I start a task in the background and wait for it later in the same playbook?
How do I check an async job's status until it finishes?
Why does my async_status task fail saying the job can't be found?
Why do my async tasks always show as changed?
How can I run async tasks in batches so only a few run at once?

answer_card.title: Wait on an async task later with async_status
answer_card.answer_md:
Register the fire-and-forget task, then poll it with `async_status`:

```yaml
- name: Run an async task
  ansible.builtin.yum:
    name: docker-io
    state: present
  async: 1000
  poll: 0
  register: yum_sleeper

- name: Check on an async task
  async_status:
    jid: "{{ yum_sleeper.ansible_job_id }}"
  register: job_result
  until: job_result is finished
  retries: 100
  delay: 10
```

- If `async:` is too low, the check fails because the status file was never written or is gone.
- Async tasks always return changed; put `changed_when`, `creates`, etc. on the `async_status` task.
- To limit concurrency, loop over `sleep_durations | batch(2) | list` with `include_tasks`, start each batch with `poll: 0`, then loop `async_status` over `async_results.results`.
